title: D2 — physical storage contract (Delta in OneLake)
description: Machine-readable contract for how FOCUS cost data is physically materialized in OneLake. Defines the managed Delta table, physical types, write/restatement semantics, partitioning, Z-order, and the compaction service-level expectation. The Delta write, the compaction-with-metrics notebook, and the Direct Lake layout precondition all load this file and FAIL LOUDLY when reality drifts from it. Do NOT assert these targets in documentation only — this file is the spec. Version 2.0.0 changed the write from append to month-scoped replace; see writeMode.

storageMode.rationale: Decision 2: managed Delta tables, not shortcuts. Shortcuts inherit the source small-file problem and cannot be compacted or Z-ordered, so they cannot remove the $2-5M/month query ceiling. Managed Delta with daily compaction is the only option that does.

rejected.shortcut: Inherits small-file fragmentation; not compactable or Z-orderable. Same problem, different door.

table.name: Costs
table.note: Column set and FOCUS version are owned by the D1 logical contract. This file owns only the PHYSICAL representation.

physicalTypeMapping.description: Maps each D1 logical type to the physical Delta/Spark type written to OneLake. Cost/price measures use double (FOCUS 'real'), matching the toolkit v1_2 decision to use real over decimal for performance at scale.

decimal.rationale: Toolkit Hub schema v1_2 converts cost/price measures from decimal to real (double) for query performance. The Delta layout matches that physical choice.

json.rationale: FOCUS Tags (and other JSON columns) are stored as a JSON-encoded string rather than a complex map type, because DirectLake has limited support for nested/complex types. Keeping them as strings preserves the DirectLake-readiness path (Decision 4).

writeMode.description: Each batch is treated as a FULL SNAPSHOT of every charge month it covers, and the write REPLACES those months atomically (Delta replaceWhere on the partition column) rather than appending. Cost Management restates: the open month is re-exported every day, and closed months receive later credit and amortization corrections. An append-only write multiplies BilledCost from the second run onward while every per-hop row-conservation check still balances, because each hop faithfully conserves whatever it was handed — the duplication is invisible to per-hop accounting. Replace is also idempotent on retry, so it covers the orchestration-retry case without a separate transaction identifier.
writeMode.minRestatementRowRatioNote: A restatement that writes less than this fraction of the rows it removed is rejected. replaceWhere cannot tell a genuine correction from a truncated source export, and a truncated export would silently delete good months. A month's row count effectively never halves between exports, so this floor is conservative. Set to null at the call site for an intentional historical re-scope.

rejected.append: Duplicates every restated month; the failure is silent because per-hop counts still balance.
rejected.mergeOnNaturalKey: Azure FOCUS has no reliable natural key. A synthesized hash key would have to be PROVEN unique against real exports before it could be trusted, and is more expensive at scale than replacing whole months. Revisit only if batches ever become partial within a month.

ingestionLedger.description: Append-only record of every restatement, so a destructive replace is auditable after the fact rather than inferred from Delta history. One row per write.

partitioning.description: Partition by charge period month. Aligns with the dominant time-range filter in cost reporting and keeps partition counts bounded.
partitioning.derivation: x_ChargeMonth = date_trunc('month', ChargePeriodStart), stored as a DATE for partition pruning.
partitioning.note: ChargePeriodStart itself is high-cardinality (daily); a derived month column keeps partitions coarse.

zorder.rationale: Reasonable default: these are the most common high-cardinality filter/group dimensions in multi-account, multi-subscription cost analysis.
zorder.validationRequired: Confirm against the pilot customer's ACTUAL dominant query filters before locking in (Phase 6). Treat as provisional until one full billing cycle of query telemetry exists. Re-running OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY with different columns is non-destructive, so this is safe to revise.
zorder.subscriptionIdNote: FOCUS 1.2 names the subscription-level scope SubAccountId. Updated from the provisional SubscriptionId placeholder.

compaction.description: Compaction is treated as a MONITORED SLA, not a fire-and-forget scheduled job. It is load-bearing for query performance AND for the DirectLake-readiness gate, and is the easiest thing to silently stop running.

sla.note: 26h tolerance allows one missed daily window before alerting. Breaching any threshold must raise an alert (Data Activator / monitoring), not silently degrade queries. These are PRODUCTION thresholds; a small pilot/test dataset that cannot reach the 64MB floor should pass pilot-scale sla_overrides to validate_compaction_sla at the call site (see 03_compaction) rather than lowering these values.

metrics.description: Emitted on every run to a location an alert can watch. These are the inputs to both the SLA check and the Direct Lake layout precondition. File counts and sizes MUST be measured over the Delta log's ACTIVE file set: OPTIMIZE does not delete the files it supersedes, so a plain listing of the table location counts both generations and reports a freshly compacted table as fragmented.
metrics.bytesRewrittenNote: Bytes OPTIMIZE actually wrote, taken from the operation's own filesAdded metrics. NOT the table's total size — those differ by orders of magnitude on an incremental compaction, and reporting the latter makes a no-op run look like a full rewrite.

sink.name: _pilot_compaction_metrics
sink.note: Append-only operational table; one row per run. Watchable by Data Activator or a scheduled alert query.

directLake.description: Guardrails consumed by the Direct Lake layout precondition (Decision 4). Direct Lake silently falls back to DirectQuery above these limits, so they are checked, not assumed. These values are DELIBERATELY UNSET: the limits vary by Fabric capacity SKU, and a built-in default is wrong for most capacities in both directions — a permissive default produces a false pass on a small SKU, which is precisely the silent failure this gate exists to prevent. Look up the limits published for YOUR capacity SKU and record them here. The notebook fails loudly while they are null.
directLake.note: Set minAvgFileSizeMB to at least the compaction SLA floor so a table that passes compaction is also sized appropriately for Direct Lake memory-mapping. Re-check all three on any capacity resize.
directLake.scopeNote: These cover table LAYOUT only. Clearing them does not establish that a Direct Lake semantic model will perform: relationships, one-side uniqueness, RLS/OLS and fixed identity, framing, cold-query latency, memory pressure, and observed fallback are all model-level and are not evaluated here.

rowConservation.description: The rows a materialization hop WRITES must equal the rows it READ. Real hub failures change that count with NO error: extents silently lost during multi-file ingestion, or rows dropped when a manifest row count is null. The notebooks capture the input and output counts of each hop and hand them to validate_row_conservation, which fails loudly on any drift beyond the tolerance below.
rowConservation.note: 0.0 means exact conservation (input count must equal output count). This governs the ROWS MOVED BY THE HOP, not the table total: a month-scoped replace legitimately removes prior rows for the months it restates, and that removal is recorded in the ingestion ledger and bounded by writeMode.minRestatementRowRatio rather than by this rule. KQL remains the single transform owner (Decision 1), so no hop should add or drop rows in transit. Raise this only if a hop legitimately dedupes or filters, and document why.

batchHandoff.description: Ingestion (notebook 01) and the Delta write (notebook 02) run as separate executions connected only by staging files in OneLake, whose listing can lag (see README OneLake sync notes). A partial staging read in notebook 02 would still pass that notebook's own row-conservation check because it conserves whatever subset it read — the loss is silent. This is the cross-boundary form of the #1625 / #2173 'processed a subset, assumed the whole' trap. To close it, notebook 01 writes an authoritative batch manifest (expected row count) and notebook 02 asserts, via validate_batch_completeness, that it consumed exactly that many rows before writing anything to Delta.
batchHandoff.note: Mirrors how the toolkit hub uses manifest.json row counts — the exact mechanism issue #2173 shows failing when the count is null. The manifest count is authoritative, so completeness is an exact-equality check with no tolerance.

enforcement.description: Policy applied by the Delta write, the compaction notebook, and the layout precondition. Every rule maps to a silent-failure scenario from the decision deck.
